title: Introduce presubmit cost tagging and release sanity prober
author: Claire Wong
description: Motivation: our presubmit lanes have become cost-opaque as we add more integration smoke checks and cross-repo dependency probes. This leads to surprising billing spikes and makes it hard to tune fast-feedback lanes. This PR adds two complementary capabilities: 1) a lightweight presubmit cost tagging system that annotates presubmit runs with an estimated token/CPU/GPU cost bucket so owners can see marginal cost of changes in CI, and 2) a release sanity prober service (local simulator + optional cluster job) that runs a small deterministic set of smoke flows against the release orchestration hooks to validate that a scheduled rollout will not trigger cascading CI bursts. The description below is intentionally single-stream: Changes: - Introduce presubmit-cost-tagging: a small step in our presubmit runner that samples job durations and resource labels, maps them into one of five cost buckets (free, low, medium, high, extreme), and attaches a lightweight annotation to PR checks and the console dashboard. The estimator uses historical metrics (from observability pipeline) for the job signature plus simple heuristics for new jobs. - Add release-sanity-prober: a Kubernetes Job + local simulator binary (cmd/release-prober) that replays a compact set of release hooks (canary deploy, autoscale spike, fallback to variant) against a mirrored staging pipeline to detect if new changes increase the probability of triggering broad-scale CI. The simulator can run in 'dry' mode and output a delta cost estimate for the upcoming release window. - Console/ui: a minimal integration that surfaces presubmit cost bucket in the PR checks summary, and a release-prober panel under the Release Dashboard showing recent probe runs and deltas. - Telemetry/telemetry docs: new events (ci.presubmit.cost_bucket, ci.release_prober.delta) and a dashboard to trace cost-impact per PR. - Rollout plan: gated rollout to 30% of presubmit runners for 48 hours, then full enable. For release-prober we deploy to staging first and make cluster opt-in. Checklist: - [x] Presubmit tagging added to runner and annotator (pkg/ci/annotator). - [x] Release prober binary + CRD shim for cluster runs (cmd/release-prober, k8s/). - [x] Console integration + small React panel (web/console/src/components/ReleaseProberPanel.tsx). - [x] Telemetry metrics and dashboards (observability/dashboards/release-prober). - [x] Tests: unit tests for estimator, integration smoke tests for simulator. How it works: presubmit runs are sampled (1/10 default) for full profiling; for non-sampled runs we use signature-based lookup to infer bucket. The estimator prefers historical medians but falls back to static heuristics to avoid instability. Release prober runs a short scenario trace (<= 20s per scenario) that exercises routing and rollout logic; it outputs an aggregated expected CI event delta. Usage notes: - Local dev: make dev-prober (builds binary) and ./_bin/release-prober --simulate --profile=my-change - To run a cluster probe: kubectl apply -f k8s/release-prober-job.yaml - Console supports filter by cost_bucket and shows last 7 probe deltas. Security notes: prober uses readonly tokens and cannot trigger production rollouts. Performance: sampling is conservative and opt-out per-repo via repo config. Migration: add opt-in flag to .redwood/ci.yml, default: false. Observability: new SLI to track average presubmit cost per PR and a regression alert when median presubmit cost for main increases >15% over a 7-day baseline.
commits: 3 commits: 1) add presubmit cost estimator and annotator (pkg/ci/estimator, pkg/ci/annotator) 2) implement release-prober binary and k8s job shim (cmd/release-prober, k8s/release-prober-job.yaml) 3) console panel and telemetry wiring (web/console, observability/dashboards). Commits are small and focused; unit tests and basic integration test included.
review_comments: Evan Brooks: This is compelling — a couple of asks: can the cost buckets be overridden per-repo and can we include a raw estimated token/second number for better transparency?
Claire Wong (author): Yes — added repo opt-out flag and a repo-level override map. We also added a raw_estimate field in telemetry and console tooltips.
Maya Singh: I worry about probe runtime load in staging; can we add a throttle and backoff? Also add a guard so prober job cannot launch more than one concurrent job per namespace.
Claire Wong (author): Implemented throttle (cluster sidecar limiter + local flag) and concurrency guard on the job CRD. Tests included to validate single-run semantics.
Diego Alvarez: CI flake on Windows runner for build of cmd/release-prober; suggests switching to go 1.21 build tags to skip syscall-specific bits.
Claire Wong (author): Reworked small syscall usage and added cross-platform CI job matrix. Rerun CI and green.
release_notes: Add presubmit cost tagging (estimates per-PR) and a release sanity prober to simulate release-window CI impact. Opt-in per-repo. Improves visibility into presubmit cost and helps detect rollout-triggered CI bursts before production.
post_merge_actions: migrations: add ci.presubmit.cost_bucket keystore entry; ops: enable opt-in flag for 30% of runners via feature flag. Docs: see docs/ci/presubmit-costs.md for owner and opt-out steps.
ci_log_summary: Initial CI run: lint/test matrix failed on windows build (fixed), rerun: all checks passed (unit/integration/console-lint). Coverage delta: -0.03% (within tolerance).
notes_for_release: Ship in next minor (no breaking changes). Feature is opt-in; recommend enabling for busy teams and enabling release-prober in staging before enabling on main.
estimated_risks: Low. Prober is read-only by default and presubmit sampling default is conservative. Main risk is increased billing when teams turn on prober or change sampling rate — mitigated by feature flag and cost buckets visible in PRs.
